children: Australian shares edged lower on Monday as miners' losses outweighed bank gains, with investors bracing for a possible fifth rate hike this year.
The S&P/ASX 200 index
fell 0.2% to 8,894.10 by 2343 GMT. The benchmark rose 1.3% last week.
Miners
fell 1.5%, as sector heavyweights came under pressure from the recent weakness in iron ore and copper prices.
BHP
slid 1.3%. Rio Tinto
fell 1.4%, extending Friday's losses after it reported that a seismic event temporarily disrupted underground mining at its Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia.
Gold sub-index
dropped 2.8% after bullion fell to a one-year low in the previous session.
Consumer staples (.AXSJ) dropped 1.9%, after falling 5% last week, with major grocers
and Coles
down around 3%.
Among the few bright spots were financials
, which rose 0.5%, helped by a 1% advance by Westpac (.WBC.AX).
The lender reported a marginal rise in its full-year profit, supported by healthy growth in deposits and lending while mortgage demand slowed.
The remaining three of the big four banks posted gains of 0.2% to 0.5%.
The high-yielding sector recouped most of its 7% August-September losses last month as investors sought safety amid a global tech rout and rate worries.
Technology stocks
declined 1.5%, tracking a sharp drop in the Nasdaq on Friday amid renewed concerns over heavy AI spending.
The potential for still higher domestic borrowing costs continued to weigh on sentiment.
Above-target inflation and Governor Michele Bullock's hawkish comments last week have led many economists to shift their forecasts to a rate hike at Tuesday's policy meeting.
All but two of 32 economists polled by Reuters now expect the cash rate to rise to 4.85%.
